title: Feeder upgrades that need their substation

blocks.text: An electric cooperative is rebuilding a substation (project `SUB`). Four feeder upgrades (`F1` to `F4`) hang off it: each one is only worth doing if the substation is rebuilt, but the substation may be rebuilt with any number of its feeders, none included. This is a one-period selection: each project is funded or not.
A colleague wrote the rule in `add_aggregated_needs` as one row for all the children together. It allows exactly the right whole-number plans, but the LP bound of the planning model is loose.

Write `add_parent_rows(model, x, parent, children)` in `feeders.py`: the same rule, written so that the LP relaxation cannot fund a valuable feeder on a small fraction of the substation. `x[pid]` is each project's variable.
The model so far, with $`p`$ the parent, $`C`$ its children and the colleague's row shown for comparison:
Write your rows in this notation first, each with its quantifier and a label, then code them. Check them against a plan with only the substation, and against a plan with two feeders.

The tests fix a plan by its variables' bounds and ask the solver whether it is allowed, so any correct set of rows passes; one more test checks that on a small LP your rows give a smaller LP value (a tighter bound: for a maximization the LP value bounds every plan from above) than the colleague's. About three lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
from datetime import timedelta

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt

from feeders import Project, add_parent_rows, selection_variables

def solve_ok(model):
    params = mathopt.SolveParameters(time_limit=timedelta(seconds=5))
    result = mathopt.solve(model, mathopt.SolverType.HIGHS, params=params)
    return result.termination.reason == mathopt.TerminationReason.OPTIMAL


def allowed(plan):
    model = mathopt.Model()
    x = selection_variables(model, [Project(pid, 5, 1) for pid in ["HUB", "L1", "L2", "L3"]])
    add_parent_rows(model, x, "HUB", ["L1", "L2", "L3"])
    for pid, var in x.items():
        var.lower_bound = var.upper_bound = 1.0 if pid in plan else 0.0
    return solve_ok(model)


print("plan HUB:", allowed({"HUB"}))
print("plan HUB L1 L3:", allowed({"HUB", "L1", "L3"}))
print("plan L2:", allowed({"L2"}))
print("plan L1 L2:", allowed({"L1", "L2"}))

origin.section: Disaggregated Is Stronger, Not Always Bigger

concepts: a parent rule over several children can be written in more than one form, and the forms can allow the same whole-number plans
how the number of rows in a form trades against the strength of its LP bound
